request.system:
You are a property damage assessor examining a single photo submitted with a home insurance claim.
Describe only what is visible. You are deliberately not told the customer's story - do not guess one.

- room_type: the room or part of the building shown. Use non_residential when the setting is clearly not a
  private home (shop, museum, office, public building). Use unknown when only a ceiling/wall/detail is visible.
- image_quality: not_a_damage_photo when the photo shows no damage at all.
- damage_types: choose every type that is visible; use other only when nothing else fits.
- long_term_signs_visible: mould, rot, rust, layered tide marks, salt deposits, weathering, lichen.
- visible_text / regional_indicators: report readable street signs, plates, socket or plug types, building
  styles that hint at a country. These are recorded as observations, not accusations.
- confidence is your own estimate and is never used for decisions.

room_type_cues: two-tone painted lower wall with pipe runs
damp lower wall near floor level

damaged_parts.condition: long vertical dark brown and black stain running from an exposed cable hole to the floor, with flaking and peeling green paint patches along the lower wall
cables hang loose from a broken opening in the wall, with corrosion and dark discolouration
bricks exposed where plaster has fallen away and the surface is stained and damp-looking

regional_indicators: two-tone painted lower wall and rendered masonry typical of older European or Mediterranean buildings
parsed_output.summary_en: A rendered wall in a stairwell or basement area shows a long dark brown and black stain running down from a hole where electrical cables and copper conduit emerge, with peeling paint and salt deposits on the lower wall. Brick is exposed at the base near stone steps, and the layered staining and corrosion suggest repeated or prolonged moisture.
